lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That night, the Lord says: arise, go down to the camp. I have given it into your hand.

lines.speaker: gideon
lines.text: If you will save Israel by my hand, let this be the sign: a fleece of dew, a bowl of water.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Gideon goes down with Purah, his servant, to the edge of the armed camp. The Midianites are countless, their camels like sand.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In a tent, a soldier tells his friend a dream: a barley cake tumbled into the camp, struck the tent, and it lay flat.

lines.speaker: midianite_soldier
lines.text: This is nothing but the sword of Gideon. God has given the Midianites and their camp into his hand.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Gideon hears the dream and its meaning. He worships, then returns to his camp and gives the order: arise, the Lord has given them into your hand.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The dream is not Gideon's, and the falling tent is not a real attack. It is a whisper the enemy spoke against itself.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The overheard assurance settles. The route was an adaptation — it cannot change the outcome. What remains is trust.

choices.label: Return to the three hundred
choices.note: The story keeps its shape; Gideon carries the assurance forward.

choices.label: Rest at the camp's edge
choices.note: A pause does not change the outcome. It only lets the player breathe.
